description: The provided pie chart visually organizes the core principles of medical ethics into four primary domains — Beneficence, Non-Maleficence, Autonomy, and Justice — each represented by a distinct color and subdivided into specific ethical obligations or duties. The largest segment, Beneficence (blue), encompasses a wide range of responsibilities including providing medical care, continual learning, respecting patient dignity, minimizing conflicts of interest, ethical research, and fair charging of fees. Non-Maleficence (purple) focuses on preventing harm, maintaining qualifications, reporting unethical conduct, and avoiding personal gain from medicine. Autonomy (green) emphasizes patient rights such as informed consent, freedom of choice, truthful communication, confidentiality, and the physician’s right to choose whom to serve. Justice (orange) addresses fairness in allocating medical resources, treating patients equitably, promoting public health and environmental sustainability. The chart uses a radial layout with labeled slices radiating outward from the central ethical principles, offering a structured, hierarchical view of medical ethical duties without numerical percentages, relying instead on relative visual proportions to convey emphasis. This visualization likely serves as a conceptual framework for evaluating how well large language models (LLMs) understand and reason about medical ethics, as referenced in the paper “MedEthicsQA: A Comprehensive Question Answering Benchmark for Medical Ethics Evaluation of LLMs.”
